biography: Stéphane Ratel, a name whispered with respect and a touch of apprehension in the GT racing world, hails from the sun-drenched fields of Provence, France. Unlike many of his peers who were practically born in go-karts, Stéphane’s introduction to motorsport was relatively late, sparked by a chance encounter with a retired rally driver while working on his family's vineyard. The smell of high-octane fuel and the roar of engines ignited a passion that quickly consumed him. His early years were marked by relentless dedication, honing his skills in local karting competitions before making the jump to single-seaters. A defining moment came at the 24 Hours of Spa where, despite a mechanical failure in the final hour, his blistering pace and tactical acumen had already cemented his reputation as a force to be reckoned with. Now at the peak of his career, driving for Blu Corse, Stéphane is a constant threat for podium finishes, meticulously analyzing every variable to gain an edge.
drivingStyle: Ratel's driving style is best described as calculating aggression. He doesn't bulldoze his way through the field; instead, he patiently observes, identifying weaknesses in his opponents and exploiting them with surgical precision. His corner entry is deceptively smooth, allowing him to carry maximum speed through the apex and maintain momentum. Tire management is a particular strength; he possesses an almost uncanny ability to conserve rubber without sacrificing pace, often setting fastest laps in the closing stages of a race when others are struggling. Under pressure, he remains ice-cold, rarely cracking under the intense scrutiny of a close battle.

famousQuote: "Racing isn't just about speed; it's about strategy. It's a chess game played at 300 kilometers per hour."
careerHighlight: Winning the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2028, a hard-fought victory that solidified his status as one of the sport's elite endurance racers, battling through torrential rain and mechanical issues to take the checkered flag.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the final lap of the Spa 24 Hours in 2027 due to a sudden downpour, a devastating blow that left him questioning his judgment and approach.
